title: Project PRD / Brief Template
subtitle: Agentic-first documentation foundation for product, design, and engineering alignment.

hero.lead: Use this template as a living product source of truth. It is structured for both human collaboration and AI-assisted planning, critique, and execution.

sections.title: Project Overview & Document Information
sections.summary: Record the document identity, ownership, and linked artifacts so every contributor is aligned on source references.

fields.label: Project Title
fields.description: Concise, descriptive name of the project.

fields.label: Document Owner
fields.description: Your name, team, or accountable owner group.

fields.label: Version
fields.description: Use semantic increments like v1.0, v1.1.

fields.label: Related Documents
fields.description: Attach links to design mockups, research findings, technical design docs, and business models.

sections.title: Executive Summary (The Brief in a Nutshell)
sections.summary: Capture the one-screen context any stakeholder should understand before reading details.

fields.label: What is this project?
fields.description: Very brief, high-level description of the core deliverable.

fields.label: Why are we doing it?
fields.description: Summarize the problem or opportunity and expected strategic impact.

fields.label: What is the expected outcome?
fields.description: Define visible success indicators such as conversion lift, churn reduction, or market entry.

sections.title: Background & Context
sections.summary: Explain the current state and strategic alignment so the project is anchored in evidence, not intuition.

cards.title: Current State
cards.body: Describe the existing system or process this project addresses or replaces.
cards.meta: Include user and business pain points

cards.title: Supporting Data
cards.body: List metrics, tickets, feedback, and qualitative signals that validate urgency.
cards.meta: Examples: low conversion, high support volume

cards.title: Strategic Alignment
cards.body: Map to company goals, product strategy, or active OKRs.

sections.title: Problem Statement / Opportunity
sections.summary: Write a specific and testable problem statement, then articulate the upside unlocked by solving it.
list: What exactly is broken or missing?
When and where does it happen in the user journey?
What is the measurable impact (revenue loss, churn, inefficiency, risk)?
sections.callout: Example problem: Our checkout flow causes 30% of mobile users to abandon carts due to complex form fields, resulting in an estimated $50k/month in lost revenue.
sections.secondaryCallout: Example opportunity: A social sharing feature could increase viral growth by 15%, leading to 10,000 new sign-ups per month.

sections.title: Goals & Objectives (SMART Metrics)
sections.summary: Define measurable targets and tie every goal to instrumentation plans.

cards.title: Project Goal
cards.body: Increase mobile checkout conversion rate by 10% within 3 months post-launch.

cards.title: Project Goal
cards.body: Reduce support tickets related to account settings by 25% within 6 weeks post-launch.

sections.title: Target Audience / Users
sections.summary: Specify who gets value, who is impacted, and who supports delivery decisions.

fields.label: Primary Users
fields.description: Demographics, behaviors, needs, and pain points relevant to this initiative.

fields.label: Secondary Users / Stakeholders
fields.description: Internal or adjacent groups affected by rollout, such as support, sales, admins, or operations.

sections.title: Solution Overview
sections.summary: Describe the solution in plain language and connect it to problem resolution and business value.

cards.title: High-Level Solution
cards.body: Redesign mobile checkout to a single-page progressive form with auto-fill and clear progress states.

cards.title: Value Proposition
cards.body: Deliver faster completion for users and increased conversion for the business.

sections.title: Scope & Deliverables
sections.summary: Define boundaries so teams can execute quickly without scope ambiguity.

rows: Features and components explicitly included in delivery (e.g., redesigned mobile checkout + payment gateway integration).
Non-goals to avoid expectation drift (e.g., desktop redesign, new payment methods).
Concrete outputs such as app versions, APIs, analytics dashboards, documentation.

sections.title: Detailed Requirements (Features & Functionality)
sections.summary: Translate intent into testable stories and functional behaviors.

fields.label: User Stories
fields.description: Use the format: As a [user], I want to [action], so that [benefit].

fields.label: Prioritization
fields.description: Assign each item by priority scale (High/Medium/Low or MoSCoW).

fields.label: Functional Requirements
fields.description: Document explicit system behaviors such as validation, encryption, and workflow logic.

list: As a mobile user, I want a clear progress indicator so I know how many steps remain. (High)
As a returning customer, I want shipping details pre-filled so checkout is faster. (High)
As an administrator, I want abandoned-cart details so I can follow up. (Medium)

sections.title: User Experience (UX) & User Interface (UI)
sections.summary: Document primary journeys, design principles, and accessibility standards.

fields.label: Design Principles
fields.description: State principles such as simplicity, accessibility, and consistency.

fields.label: Wireframes/Mockups/Prototypes
fields.description: Attach links to Figma, prototypes, and usability test outcomes.

fields.label: Accessibility Considerations
fields.description: Specify WCAG level, keyboard support, semantic structure, and screen reader behavior.

sections.title: Technical Requirements & Considerations
sections.summary: Capture architecture, integrations, quality constraints, and telemetry from the start.

cards.title: Architecture & Infrastructure
cards.body: Outline new services, major system changes, and deployment model impacts.

cards.title: Integrations
cards.body: List internal and external systems, contracts, and dependencies.

cards.title: Performance
cards.body: Define latency targets, throughput, and scalability requirements.

cards.title: Security
cards.body: Set encryption, authentication, authorization, and vulnerability requirements.

cards.title: Data Model & APIs
cards.body: Track schema changes and new/updated API surfaces.

cards.title: Analytics
cards.body: Define KPI event tracking for tools like Amplitude or Google Analytics.

sections.title: Dependencies & Risks
sections.summary: Map dependency constraints and quantify major risks with mitigation plans.

rows: Run technical spike early to de-risk

sections.title: Release Plan & Post-Launch
sections.summary: Define rollout strategy, operational readiness, rollback safety, and KPI review cadence.
list: Phased rollout strategy: beta, gradual percentage, geo-specific
Go-to-market plan: marketing, sales enablement, support training
Monitoring and alerting plan for feature health
Rollback plan for critical launch issues
Success measurement window and review dates

sections.title: Team & Stakeholders
sections.summary: Name responsible owners, contributors, and approval roles.

sections.title: Open Questions & Assumptions
sections.summary: Track unresolved decisions and explicit assumptions that could invalidate the plan.

cards.title: Open Questions
cards.body: List unresolved details requiring investigation, decisions, or alignment.

cards.title: Assumptions
cards.body: Document assumptions that, if false, could impact scope, timeline, or outcomes.

sections.title: Appendix (Optional)
sections.summary: Keep deep context in one place without overloading the main decision narrative.

usage.title: How to Use This Template
steps: Fill it out with your project context. Start with Overview, Problem, Goals, and Solution before deep detail.
Be concise but thorough. Include enough evidence for confident decisions.
Treat it as a living document. Update whenever assumptions, requirements, or constraints change.
Collaborate early with stakeholders and cross-functional partners to maintain alignment.
